  <section id="welcome-to-langchain">
<h1>
Welcome to LangChain
<a class="headerlink" href="#welcome-to-langchain" title="Permalink to this headline">#</a>
</h1>
<p>Large language models (LLMs) are emerging as a transformative technology, enabling
developers to build applications that they previously could not.
But using these LLMs in isolation is often not enough to
create a truly powerful app - the real power comes when you are able to
combine them with other sources of computation or knowledge.</p>
<p>This library is aimed at assisting in the development of those types of applications. Common examples of these types of applications include:</p>
<p>
<strong>❓ Question Answering over specific documents</strong>
</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./use_cases/question_answering.html">Documentation</a>
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
End-to-end Example: 
<a class="reference external" href="https://github.com/hwchase17/notion-qa">Question Answering over Notion Database</a>
</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p>
<strong>💬 Chatbots</strong>
</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./use_cases/chatbots.html">Documentation</a>
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
End-to-end Example: 
<a class="reference external" href="https://github.com/hwchase17/chat-langchain">Chat-LangChain</a>
</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p>
<strong>🤖 Agents</strong>
</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./use_cases/agents.html">Documentation</a>
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
End-to-end Example: 
<a class="reference external" href="https://huggingface.co/spaces/JavaFXpert/Chat-GPT-LangChain">GPT+WolframAlpha</a>
</p>
</li>
</ul>
<section id="getting-started">
<h2>
Getting Started
<a class="headerlink" href="#getting-started" title="Permalink to this headline">#</a>
</h2>
<p>Checkout the below guide for a walkthrough of how to get started using LangChain to create an Language Model application.</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./getting_started/getting_started.html">Getting Started Documentation</a>
</p>
</li>
</ul>
<div class="toctree-wrapper compound" id="id3">
</div>
</section>
<section id="modules">
<h2>
Modules
<a class="headerlink" href="#modules" title="Permalink to this headline">#</a>
</h2>
<p>There are several main modules that LangChain provides support for.
For each module we provide some examples to get started, how-to guides, reference docs, and conceptual guides.
These modules are, in increasing order of complexity:</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./modules/prompts.html">Prompts</a>
: This includes prompt management, prompt optimization, and prompt serialization.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./modules/llms.html">LLMs</a>
: This includes a generic interface for all LLMs, and common utilities for working with LLMs.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./modules/document_loaders.html">Document Loaders</a>
: This includes a standard interface for loading documents, as well as specific integrations to all types of text data sources.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./modules/utils.html">Utils</a>
: Language models are often more powerful when interacting with other sources of knowledge or computation. This can include Python REPLs, embeddings, search engines, and more. LangChain provides a large collection of common utils to use in your application.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./modules/chains.html">Chains</a>
: Chains go beyond just a single LLM call, and are sequences of calls (whether to an LLM or a different utility). LangChain provides a standard interface for chains, lots of integrations with other tools, and end-to-end chains for common applications.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./modules/indexes.html">Indexes</a>
: Language models are often more powerful when combined with your own text data - this module covers best practices for doing exactly that.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./modules/agents.html">Agents</a>
: Agents involve an LLM making decisions about which Actions to take, taking that Action, seeing an Observation, and repeating that until done. LangChain provides a standard interface for agents, a selection of agents to choose from, and examples of end to end agents.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./modules/memory.html">Memory</a>
: Memory is the concept of persisting state between calls of a chain/agent. LangChain provides a standard interface for memory, a collection of memory implementations, and examples of chains/agents that use memory.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./modules/chat.html">Chat</a>
: Chat models are a variation on Language Models that expose a different API - rather than working with raw text, they work with messages. LangChain provides a standard interface for working with them and doing all the same things as above.
</p>
</li>
</ul>
<div class="toctree-wrapper compound" id="id4">
</div>
</section>
<section id="use-cases">
<h2>
Use Cases
<a class="headerlink" href="#use-cases" title="Permalink to this headline">#</a>
</h2>
<p>The above modules can be used in a variety of ways. LangChain also provides guidance and assistance in this. Below are some of the common use cases LangChain supports.</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./use_cases/agents.html">Agents</a>
: Agents are systems that use a language model to interact with other tools. These can be used to do more grounded question/answering, interact with APIs, or even take actions.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./use_cases/chatbots.html">Chatbots</a>
: Since language models are good at producing text, that makes them ideal for creating chatbots.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./use_cases/combine_docs.html">Data Augmented Generation</a>
: Data Augmented Generation involves specific types of chains that first interact with an external datasource to fetch data to use in the generation step. Examples of this include summarization of long pieces of text and question/answering over specific data sources.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./use_cases/question_answering.html">Question Answering</a>
: Answering questions over specific documents, only utilizing the information in those documents to construct an answer. A type of Data Augmented Generation.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./use_cases/summarization.html">Summarization</a>
: Summarizing longer documents into shorter, more condensed chunks of information. A type of Data Augmented Generation.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./use_cases/evaluation.html">Evaluation</a>
: Generative models are notoriously hard to evaluate with traditional metrics. One new way of evaluating them is using language models themselves to do the evaluation. LangChain provides some prompts/chains for assisting in this.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./use_cases/generate_examples.html">Generate similar examples</a>
: Generating similar examples to a given input. This is a common use case for many applications, and LangChain provides some prompts/chains for assisting in this.
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="./use_cases/model_laboratory.html">Compare models</a>
: Experimenting with different prompts, models, and chains is a big part of developing the best possible application. The ModelLaboratory makes it easy to do so.
</p>
</li>
</ul>

</div>
</section>

<ul class="simple">
<li>
<p>
<a class="reference external" href="https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain-hub">LangChainHub</a>

</p>

</p>
</li>

<p>

</p>
</li>
